classes.Benchmark: Frozen population identity, not an application-validation claim
classes.AccuracyRequirement: Boundary, invariant, precision, stochastic, or error requirement
classes.Implementation: CUDA.jl, KA, or JACC program at a source revision
classes.Environment: Julia language, package, toolkit and hardware identities
classes.Configuration: Named fixture, size, precision and timing scope
classes.VerificationEvidence: Recorded checked outputs and acceptance contract
classes.FailureEvent: Observed phase/candidate/check defect or explicit nonfailure observation
classes.ExecutionMeasurement: Five trials and last-four mean, distinct from profiles
classes.Hypothesis: A proposed mechanism, distinct from measured fact
classes.ScientificDomain: Reviewed domain or explicit domain-neutral classification

record_serialization: domains/<benchmark>.json and implementations/<benchmark>/<model>.json are nested annotations with explicit IDs and evidence links; no OWL inference engine is claimed.
causality_rule: A motif or domain assignment does not establish a measured bottleneck or causal abstraction cost. A causal claim needs a scoped intervention and relevant counters/timing evidence.
unknown_rule: Null records are not absent capabilities, zero costs or verified scientific mappings.
multi_domain_rule: Retain secondary scientific domains and operator roles; choose one explicit primary family for non-overlapping population counts. Review all source evidence before publishing family-count conclusions.
failure_counts_rule: Count event IDs once. Normalized events link preserved raw records rather than duplicating their counts; failures, diagnostics, repairs, affected programs and final outcomes remain distinct.
